key_insight: The paper shows that two-qubit concurrence and three-qubit 3-tangle can be directly extracted from quantum-circuit measurement probabilities using unitary operations and ancilla qubits.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical hardware-friendly route to quantify entanglement without full state tomography, reducing measurement overhead for quantum communication and quantum computing experiments.
method: Add auxiliary qubits to the target state.
Apply specific controlled unitary transformations that encode entanglement formulas into output probabilities.
Measure the ancilla/output probabilities to infer concurrence or 3-tangle directly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports proposed quantum-circuit schemes for direct quantitative measurement of bipartite concurrence and tripartite 3-tangle, avoiding full state tomography.
watch_item: The approach is presented for pure two-qubit and three-qubit states, so extending it to mixed states and noisy hardware will likely require additional calibration and validation.
paper_title: Entanglement Detection for Two-Qubit and Three-Qubit Pure States via Unitary Transformations and Ancilla State Measurements
